da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: knot-formula-table.md: the block writes `\mathfrak{u} = T_{2,3}`, `\mathfrak{d} = T_{2,3}^{\sigma}`, `\mathfrak{s} = T_{2,5}^{\sigma}`, `\mathfrak{c} = T_{2,5}`, `\mathfrak{b} = T_{2,7}^{\sigma}` — using the sigma superscript as the up-type -> down-type partner map (present iff down-type, 5/5 quark rows). But braids-and-knots/knot-notation-convention.md DEFINES the same superscript on a knot as charge conjugation: "The superscript distinguishes a particle from its antiparticle via mirror reflection (charge conjugation)", with "mirror image T_{m,n}^{\sigma} = T_{m,-n}" and the lepton instance electron T_{2,3} / positron T_{2,3}^{\sigma}. Under the DEFINED meaning these rows assert d = u-bar, s = c-bar, b = t-bar, identifying charge -1/3 quarks with charge -2/3 antiquarks. One superscript carries two relations and only the unusable one is defined. || SECOND, INDEPENDENT: the same block writes `\mathfrak{d} = T_{2,3}^{\sigma}` and then one sentence later "Here \mathfrak{d} denotes the three-twist knot 5_2". T_{2,3}^{\sigma} is the mirror trefoil 3_1 (3 crossings, a torus knot); 5_2 is a twist knot with 5 crossings and is not a torus knot at all. The block's own Table 2 row `| Down quark | \mathfrak{d} | T_{2,3}^{\sigma} | 1 | 3 |` gives Crossings = 3, agreeing with the formula and contradicting the prose.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: SUPERSEDES my own fail entry of 2026-08-24T17:20/17:30Z on the sigma question. That entry claimed sigma CANNOT be the T3 grading because knot-notation-convention.md documents it as charge conjugation, and that the discriminating assignment is 'undefined'. THAT IS WRONG. lean/QOU/ParticleInteractions/MesonOperatorSelectionT3.lean already formalises exactly this grading: `signedWrithe : Quark -> Z` gives up=3, charm=5, top=7, down=-3, strange=-5, bottom=-7; `genWinding = |signedWrithe|`; `T3 = sign(signedWrithe)/2`. Since knot-notation-convention defines T_{m,n}^sigma = T_{m,-n}, the sigma superscript IS the writhe sign flip, and T3 is exactly its sign. So sigma IS the T3 grading, and it is Lean-proved to do the work: `T3_charm_ne_strange`, `graded_D_kaon_distinct` (the D/kaon collision the audit called a blocker), and `gradedContent_injective_on_dictionary`. || WHAT SURVIVES: the defect is NOT that sigma is undefined -- it is that knot-notation-convention.md:1 over-states the gloss, calling the superscript charge conjugation ('distinguishes a particle from its antiparticle via mirror reflection'). For LEPTONS the mirror does give the antiparticle (electron/positron); for QUARKS it gives the weak-isospin partner, not the antiquark. Taken literally the gloss makes d = u-bar (charge -1/3 = -2/3). The fix is to narrow the gloss to the mirror and let the physical reading depend on the sector, citing MesonOperatorSelectionT3. || The 5_2 and amphichirality findings in the prior entries are UNAFFECTED and still stand. The quark rows d=T(2,3)^sigma, s=T(2,5)^sigma, b=T(2,7)^sigma are CORRECT as written -- they encode negative signed writhe. The 5_2 defect in this block is unaffected: lepton-meson-torus-knot-dictionary.lean:27 encodes `pion: u-bar(3) + d(3) = 6`, so d contributes 3 crossings and 'the three-twist knot 5_2' (5 crossings) is the error.
da-definitional-ambiguity.notes: Self-correction. The prior entry's sigma analysis was wrong; its 5_2 / amphichirality findings stand. Analysis + options: docs/audits/2026-08-02-meson-fluxtube-junction-reduction.md; PR #5659.

da-definitional-ambiguity.evidence: The defect previously recorded on this block is FIXED. The clause 'Here d denotes the three-twist knot 5_2, which is a Skein descendant of the trefoil' is replaced by 'Here d denotes the mirror trefoil T_{2,-3}, of three crossings; the mirror marks the down-type member of the doublet, not an antiparticle.' This agrees with the block's own Table 2 row (Crossings = 3), with signedWrithe .down = -3, and with the load-bearing lepton-meson-torus-knot-dictionary.lean:27 `pion: u-bar(3) + d(3) = 6` — under the old 5_2 reading (5 crossings) the pion would be 8 and collide with the kaon. The quark rows themselves were always correct and are unchanged.
